{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This is a basic workflow to help you get started with Actions

name: Reorder

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  run:
    name: reorder
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CONFS_REORDER }}
      - name: Use Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version-file: '.nvmrc'
          cache: npm
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Reorder conferences
        run: npm run reorder-confs
      - name: Reorder valid locations
        run: npm run updateValidLocations
      - name: Commit changes
        uses: EndBug/add-and-commit@v9
        with:
          author_name: Confs.tech Reorder Bot
          author_email: cgrail@users.noreply.github.com
          message: 'Reorder conferences'
          add: \"['*.json']\"
",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs npm ci on every workflow_dispatch invocation and ships a committed package-lock.json, but the setup-node step does not enable the npm dependency cache. Evidence pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (cache dependency downloads) supports caching dependency downloads when a lockfile exists and no equivalent cache is present; both preconditions hold here and no contraindication applies (no existing cache, and npm ci with a lockfile is deterministic rather than mutable/untrusted cached content). Adding cache: npm to actions/setup-node reuses the dependency cache across runs while preserving every existing step, the checkout token, the Node version file from .nvmrc, and all build/commit coverage. It introduces no new secrets, privileged actions, deployment/publishing operations, or network access beyond the existing npm ci.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
